analysis.evidence: כִּי gives the reason for the preceding command to look around. God promises to give Abram and his descendants all the land Abram sees.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew conjunction without a prefix or suffix.
Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה רֹאֶה, “all the land that you see,” כָּל marks the full extent of the land promised to Abram and his descendants.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, with הָאָרֶץ as its complement.

analysis.evidence: The clause אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה רֹאֶה identifies the land Abram can see. God promises to give that territory to Abram and his descendants.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a common noun in the singular absolute. The noun can take either gender. Here the feminine singular object suffix in אֶתְּנֶנָּה refers back to it.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces the clause אַתָּה רֹאֶה, “you see.” Its antecedent כָּל הָאָרֶץ supplies the object of רֹאֶה, yielding “all the land that you see.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה רֹאֶה, “that you see,” אַתָּה identifies Abram as the subject of the masculine singular participle רֹאֶה. The land is what he sees.
analysis.morphology: Independent second-person masculine singular personal pronoun, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל־הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה רֹאֶה, “all the land that you see,” אַתָּה identifies Abram as the one seeing, and the land is what he can see.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, used as the predicate of אַתָּה.
